articles.headline: The Pierre Convention.
articles.text:
A special telegram from Pierre states that nothing has been done as yet except to organize.

An associated Press dispatch says: All the old leaders are on the ground and in active service for their man. Nearly all the Black Hills delegation are here and persistent for McMaster, of the Homestake mine, for delegate. McMaster has chartered the entire Grand Pacific hotel, three stories, for his delegation and friends. It is reported a combination has been entered into between Raymond and McMaster that if Raymond cannot get a sufficient vote to throw his support to McMaster.

Delegates from the following North Dakota counties stand about as follows, according to last report: Those refusing to go into the Raymond caucus: Barnes 2, Burleigh 7, Billings 2, Benson 2, Cavalier 2, Emmons 2, Grand Forks 9, Griggs 3, Logan 2, McLean 2, Mercer 2, Morton 5, Nelson 2, Ransom 3, Richland 2, Stutsman 3, Walsh 2, a total of 52 North Dakota delegates refusing to caucus.
articles.summary: Telegraphic report from the Republican territorial convention at Pierre: McMaster's Black Hills backers and 52 North Dakota delegates, Billings county's two among them, refusing to caucus for Raymond.

articles.text: The Republican territorial convention met yesterday at Pierre to nominate a delegate to congress. It is quite likely that one or two days will be occupied in effecting an organization, and that we will not learn the result before next Saturday and perhaps not until later. Indications are that a very stubborn fight will be made against the present incumbent, John B. Raymond, and the chances are that some man from South Dakota will receive the nomination. Mr. Samuel McMaster, of Deadwood, is spoken of, and may be properly termed a very prominent dark horse. The selection of Mr. McMaster as the standard bearer of the party would give very general satisfaction to the people of the territory, and particularly to the residents of the Black Hills, where he is recognized as a shrewd, active and energetic business man.
articles.summary: Editorial noting that the territorial convention met at Pierre and favoring Samuel McMaster of Deadwood over incumbent John B. Raymond.

articles.text: The Baron and Baroness von Hoffman are expected to return from their western trip in a few days.
articles.summary: The Baron and Baroness von Hoffman are expected back from a western trip.

articles.summary: Stage company superintendent Deffebach returned from Helena with eleven horses for the stage line.

articles.summary: J. C. Fisher, local manager of the stage company, has a new office partitioned off in the warehouse.

articles.text: H. M. Jorgens and Vic Smith returned yesterday from a tour of inspection over the stage route. Vic is the pathfinder, and last week discovored a route from the first station on Davis creek to the second on Rocky Ridge, which to the right follows a divide and has a natural gravel road-bed the whole distance. This route will avoid nearly one-half of the bad road on this end. Lumber for two more stations is being sent out, and stoves and other utensils have been distributed to stations already built.
articles.summary: Jorgens and Vic Smith returned from inspecting the stage route; Smith found a better route from the Davis creek station to Rocky Ridge, and lumber for two more stations is going out.

articles.headline: A Cow Boy on Skates.
articles.text:
The cow boys take to the new style of locomotion as naturally as a Democrat takes to Stonewall or Valley Tan. Toll Caldwell was telling me of the fun he had last night. He said: "I am more used to riding on horseback, but last night I thought I'd try them little wagons. I got one with a double cinch, and another one to match it, and as soon as I straddled the layout I could feel them begin to bow their backs, and I was wishing I had buckrein, because I was expectin' 'em to stiffen their knees and go to buckin' every minit, but they didn't. I walked them over to the other end of the corral to gentle 'em a little, and directly they started off at an easy canter, and were coming around back right through the herd, and there was a dude there with a stiff hat that was trying to cut out a Polled Angus heifer with a blue dress, and I fouled and roped both my hind legs with a hoop skirt and it had me stretched out for branding, quicker'n a spring calf could brawl with its mouth open and its lungs stretched. But I got up and got on again and you oughter see me exercise those vehicles. Of course they wasn't bridle wise and of course tried to buck when I hurried 'em, and they'd rear up and fall back when I tried to stop 'em too quick, but I'll leave it to the boss herder of the whole round-up if I didn't gallop 'em round there for three or four hours, and had 'em roll over with me and they didn't get me of."
—[Muldoon.
articles.summary: Humorous sketch, credited to Muldoon, of a cowboy named Toll Caldwell trying roller skates; reprinted, not a Medora event.

articles.headline: Certificate.
articles.text:
This certificate is drawn, signed and acknowledged by the parties hereto in order to conform to the requirements of the civil code of the territory of Dakota demanded of parties transacting business in said territory under a ficticious name, or under a designation not showing the names of the persons interested as partners in said business.

We the undersigned hereby certify that we have this day entered into copartnership under the name of the "Medora Stage and Forwarding Company," and that:

1. Our full and true names are Arthur T. Packard and Erasmus Deffebach.

2. That our residence is at the town of Medora, in the county of Billings, in the territory of Dakota.

3. That the principal place of business of said partnership is at the town of Medora aforesaid.

Dated, Medora, D. T., Sept. 8, 1884.
Arthur T. Packard.
Erasmus Deffebach.
Witness: Frank B. Allen.

Territory of Dakota, County of Billings, } ss.

On this eighth day of September, 1884, before me, Frank B. Allen, a notary public, personally appeared Arthur T. Packard and Erasmus Deffebach, to me well known as the same persons described in and who executed the foregoing instrument, and acknowledged that they executed the same freely and voluntarily for the uses and purposes therein expressed and specified.

In witness whereof I have hereunto set my hand and official seal at said county the day and year above written.
[Seal] Frank B. Allen, Notary Public.
articles.summary: Legal certificate of copartnership of Arthur T. Packard and Erasmus Deffebach as the Medora Stage and Forwarding Company, dated Sept. 8, 1884.

articles.text: A couple of enterprising young men of San Antonia, Tex., have undertaken to get up a car-load of heavy beeves to put on display at New Orleans during the exposition. Already several have been secured which will weigh from 1,400 to 1,700 pounds.
articles.summary: San Antonio men are assembling a carload of heavy beeves for the New Orleans exposition.

articles.text: We notice that the Standard Cattle Company, of Wyoming, have ordered fifty cars at Mingusville, Sept. 20, to accommodate their herd now on the drive for shipment. Harris & Clevinger wanted twenty cars at the same place on the 25th.—[Glendive Times.
articles.summary: Standard Cattle Company ordered fifty cars at Mingusville for Sept. 20, and Harris & Clevinger twenty for the 25th (from the Glendive Times).

articles.text: The Kansas City Drovers' News says: The Texas fever is no worse this year than it has been every summer for the past ten years, but the scare is greater because there are so many more commissioners than usual to write reports and publish articles on the subject.
articles.summary: Kansas City Drovers' News says Texas fever is no worse than usual.

articles.text: The stockmen of western and southwestern Colorado, who have been having trouble with the Utes lately, now give notice that they will shoot on sight any of the red devils caught on their ranges. The only way to get rid of them—as the government seems unable or unwilling to afford any relief.—[N. M. Stock Grower.
articles.summary: Clipping from the N. M. Stock Grower on Colorado stockmen threatening Utes found on their ranges.

articles.text: A Denver gentleman is experimenting with chemicals, for the purpose of trying to discover some more convenient and cheap method of branding than is at present used. It is claimed that more than $1,000,000 are annually lost to the cattle owners of the county by the burning of hides in branding cattle.—[N. M. Stock Grower.
articles.summary: Clipping on a Denver man experimenting with chemical branding.

articles.text: The sheep raiser must go on with his business, trying to improve his stock, to obtain more and better wool and more and better sheep, must stick close to his business, study economy, work hard, and then wait for the prosperity surely following one of the greatest periods of depression now happily passing away.—[Col. L. S. Record.
articles.summary: Clipping urging sheep raisers to persevere.

articles.text: It costs more to ship wool from Denver to the Missouri river—a distance of 550 miles—than from Melborne to Liverpool, a distance of 11,000 miles. It also costs more to ship a car load of wool from Denver to Chicago than it does to ship the same bulk and weight from San Francisco to New York and thence to London.—[Col. L. S. Record.
articles.summary: Clipping on high wool freight rates from Denver.

articles.text: Ed. Marron says he will introduce into this country the finest lot of Texas cowboys that have ever been seen around this section of the country. T. F. Burton, alias Texas, is the leader of the gang, and he is considered one of the best lariat throwers, besides being a dead shot, that the state of Texas can produce.—[Glendive Indpendent.
articles.summary: Glendive Independent clipping: Ed. Marron to bring in Texas cowboys led by T. F. Burton.

articles.text: The cattle trade with Europe is said to be declining under the influence of the Australian and Canadian competition, and if it be argued that Canada buys in the United States a good many of the cattle she sells to Great Britain, the fact remains, nevertheless, indisputable, that she ships her cargoes by her own railroads and vessels, and not by ours.—[Col. L. S. Record.
articles.summary: Clipping on declining U.S. cattle trade with Europe.

articles.text: Dorr Clark was in the city yesterday from the range. He says there are many sick cattle among some of the late through herds, but they are so effectually quarantined by the cattle men, that the disease will not be allowed to spread, if it could, to the range cattle. There has been many deaths among the afflicted herd, but it is thought the worst is now over.—[Black Hills Pioneer.
articles.summary: Black Hills Pioneer clipping: Dorr Clark reports sick cattle in late through herds, quarantined by cattlemen.

articles.text: The French government has decided to place an increased duty upon the importation of cattle, but gives such a good season for doing so that the sensible American will find more to approve than condemn in the charge. A great depression exists in the live stock interests over there, and the government regards it as "sacred duty" to assist the farmers in this way to get on their feet again.—[National Stockman.
articles.summary: Clipping on a new French duty on imported cattle.

articles.text: Old Mexico has both a herd and a lease law. An exchange says when one man's stock depredates on another's land, whether it be grass or grain, the owner is notified, if known, to take away his stock, which if not done, the animals are driven to the pound and advertised and sold. If an individual leases land in that country he knows he will get to use it, and not be compelled to pay for pasturing other people's stock.—[Exchange.
articles.summary: Clipping on Mexico's herd and lease laws.

articles.text: Official statistics of the loss of cattle in the Jonactepec district, Morelos through the excessively dry weather, are terribly suggestive of what the mortality must be for all the republic. In this district alone the figures show that 3,323 cattle and 423 horses have died this season for the lack of pasturage. The same report states that the grain crop has suffered from the ravages of a worm and from the dry weather, but no statistics are at hand to estimate the loss in grain.—[N. M. Stock Grower.
articles.summary: Clipping on drought losses of cattle in Morelos, Mexico.

articles.text: Every farmer knows that his cattle can be bred up to any attainable standard which he may choose to aim at, whether for breeding or dairying purposes; but few know how plastic their stock are in their hands. This is strictly exemplified by experiments made in breeding off the horns. If a heifer loses its horns by artificial means, and afterwards put to a horned bull, the offspring will sometimes have horns and sometimes not. By selecting the hornless ones the horns can be bred out altogether in a few generations.—[Exchange.
articles.summary: Clipping on breeding hornless cattle.

articles.text: The contagious diseases among cattle appear to be finally subsiding. The American people are equal to almost any emergency and while they are frequently caught napping, and notwithstanding the laws in many cases are yet crude and defective, they have controlled these diseases remarkably well. That such diseases actually exist no reasonable man can doubt, and once the cattlemen know that diseases actually exist they are not slow to devise ways to eradicate the same, or to at least keep them under control.—[N. W. L. S. Journal.
articles.summary: Clipping saying contagious cattle diseases are subsiding.

articles.text: The cattle brands as represented by the hundreds of oxen that freight into this city are a source of infinite amusement to the tenderfeet who study them. There are hundreds of different kinds of brands, and sometimes an individual steer will exhibit scars all over his body, from his shoulder blades to the root of his tail, to say nothing of the ear, horn and dewlap marks. A large ox stood in a team yesterday, that was as rangy and poor as they ever get, yet on his right side the expressive letters "F A T" stood out in bold relief. His mate is probably the oldest living animal in the world, that is if brands are evidence and Judge Church admits them in his court, as on his right side we saw the old time abbreviation, "B. C."—Before Christ.—[Black Hills Pioneer.
articles.summary: Black Hills Pioneer humor about brands on freighting oxen, one branded "F A T" and another "B. C."

articles.text: The profit and wealth of the cattle business may be realized in figuring up the value of the Texas drive of this year, estimated at from 500,000 to 700,000 head. At the smaller estimate $20 per head. There are $10,000,000 as the income of Texas stock owners for one year from one branch of their business only. Farmers need very much to realize this fact, which has more than usual force when the wheat crop now harvesting promises more than 500,000,000 bushels, and 75 cents a bushel seem to be a possible price. The most money made on farms henceforth will be made by the stock farmers.—[Exchange.
articles.summary: Clipping estimating the 1884 Texas drive at 500,000 to 700,000 head.

articles.text: There is a good deal of complaint in cattlemen's circles about the disposition to crowd the ranges already stocked. New men who turn cattle on the range that is occupied are the greatest sufferers, because the cattle not located are most apt to die. The located herd will live where the strangers will all pass in their checks. But this is no excuse for taking another's range. We have the reputation of sending good beef to market, but if the range crowding business goes on much longer, we can only turn off steers. The farmers of Nebraska and other Mississippi valley states will have to make the beef with their corn crop. It may prove profitable to sell steers, but beef is likely to be in greater demand, and yield to the seller a handsome profit. Don't crowd the range.—[N. W. L. S. Journal.
articles.summary: Clipping complaining about range overcrowding: "Don't crowd the range."

articles.text: Sir John Macdonald has authoritatively announced that the Canadian goverment has resolved to refuse the request of the Wyoming Stock-Growers' Association to have their stock conveyed through the dominion from the American border by the Canadian Pacific railway to Montreal for shipment to Great Britain. The premier supports his decision by charging that the scheme, if allowed, would be prejudicial to Canadian interests. The demand, he says, for cattle in England is limited, and it would be against the interest of Canadian farmers to give the stock-raisers of another country facilities to compete with them abroad. He expressed confidence from the progress already made that in a short time Canadian farmers would be amply able to supply the whole British market with beef and mutton. "Why, then," the premier urged, "should we let Wyoming ranchmen cross Canadian territory to do trade that we are prepared to do ourselves?" The first duty of the government, he held, was to encourage its own stock-raisers. The granting of the application would be adverse to their future progress. Sir John opposed any concession, lest disease break out in American cattle during transit, when the British goverment would schedule the whole continent, Canada included. These are the reasons adduced for adhering to the prohibition of American cattle coming into the Dominion.—[Breeder's Gazette.
articles.summary: Breeder's Gazette clipping: Canada refuses to let Wyoming cattle cross to Montreal by the Canadian Pacific.

articles.headline: Republican Convention.
articles.text:
Notice is hereby given that a Republican convention will be held at Medora, Dak., Monday evening, September 22, at 7 o'clock, in Roberts' hall, for the purpose of electing two delegates to represent Billings county in the legislative convention to be held at Bismarck, Dak., on the 15th of October.
J. C. Fisher, Chairman County Central Com.
articles.summary: Call for a Republican county convention at Roberts' hall, Medora, Sept. 22, to elect two delegates to the Bismarck legislative convention on Oct. 15.

articles.text: The fall round-up commenced last Monday.
articles.summary: The fall round-up began on Monday.

articles.text: E. W. Crane, of Emigrant Gulch, Mont., was in town this week.
articles.summary: E. W. Crane of Emigrant Gulch, Mont., was in town.

articles.text: Mr. Duryea, of the government surveying party, was in town yesterday.
articles.summary: Mr. Duryea of the government surveying party was in town.

articles.text: C. D. Edick, cigar manufacturer of Bismarck, was in town last week.
articles.summary: Bismarck cigar maker C. D. Edick was in town last week.

articles.text: The stage horses are being shod as rapidly as possible and distributed along the line.
articles.summary: Stage horses are being shod and sent out along the line.

articles.text: J. L. Crooks, of Spearfish, drove in this week 126 head of horses for H. R. Tarbell & Co.
articles.summary: J. L. Crooks of Spearfish drove in 126 horses for H. R. Tarbell & Co.

articles.text: T. M. Wright, formerly of the Bismarck Tribune, was in town a few days this week.
articles.summary: T. M. Wright, formerly of the Bismarck Tribune, visited Medora.

articles.text: Supt. Green, of the Missouri division, passed through on last evening's west bound passenger.
articles.summary: Northern Pacific superintendent Green passed through on the westbound train.

articles.text: The new church is to be built by the Marchioness instead of the Marquis, as stated in last week's paper.
articles.summary: Correction: the Marchioness de Morès, not the Marquis, will build the new church.

articles.text: J. A. Ferris, one of our enterprising merchants, has added a complete stock of groceries to his general store.
articles.summary: J. A. Ferris added groceries to his general store.

articles.text: Gill Kennedy is decorating the stage coaches with a coat of paint, which improves their appearance wonderfully.
articles.summary: Gill Kennedy is painting the stage coaches.

articles.text: The firm of Coleman & Brown, proprietors of the Medora hotel, have dissolved partnership, M. M. Coleman continuing the business.
articles.summary: Coleman & Brown of the Medora hotel dissolved; M. M. Coleman continues the business.

articles.text: One of the railroad carpenters went to Dickinson Sunday, and while under the influence of tanglefoot was rolled for his watch and pocket-book.
articles.summary: A railroad carpenter was robbed of his watch and pocketbook while drunk in Dickinson on Sunday.

articles.text: Dr. H. M. Jorgens is daily expecting the arrival of his drug stock. The building which he is to occupy temporarily has been moved next to the company's store.
articles.summary: Dr. H. M. Jorgens awaits his drug stock; his temporary building was moved next to the company store.

articles.text: Frank Turner is overhauling the machinery in the abattoir and will put it in first-class order. Frank is availing himself of every interval in killing to get things in shape.
articles.summary: Frank Turner is overhauling the abattoir machinery.

articles.text: We were misinformed last week in regard to the new brick cottage the Baroness von Hoffmann is building. Mr. Grymes is the happy recipient of the Baroness' valuable present.
articles.summary: Correction: the brick cottage the Baroness von Hoffmann is building is a present for Mr. Grymes.

articles.text: John Norton returned from St. Paul Tuesday evening, whither he had gone with several carloads of the company's dressed beef. He reports that they arrived in excellent condition.
articles.summary: John Norton returned from St. Paul after delivering carloads of the company's dressed beef.

articles.text: Pat. O'Hara came in from the stage route last Monday. He has the coal mine running in full blast again and is prepared to fill all orders on short notice. Leave your orders at this office.
articles.summary: Pat O'Hara came in from the stage route; his coal mine is running again.

articles.text: Remember the Republican county convention to be held at Medora hall on next monday evening, September 22, for the purpose of electing two delegates to represent Billings county in the legislative convention.
articles.summary: Reminder of the Republican county convention on Sept. 22.

articles.text: Bill Luse, an experienced stage driver of Montana, arrived in town this week. The stage company can congratulate themselves upon having secured the best and most efficient corps of stage drivers in the country.
articles.summary: Montana stage driver Bill Luse arrived to drive for the stage company.

articles.text: A new refrigerator car, the "Antartic," was loaded with beef by the company, as an experiment, and shipped in care of the builder. If this car is a success, as it promises to be, several cars will be built and put on the road.
articles.summary: The company loaded beef into an experimental refrigerator car, the "Antartic."

articles.text: New and attractive buildings are going up in every part of town, and the building boom will undoubtedly continue for the next two or the months. This is an evidence of prosperity that few towns west of the Missouri can boast of.
articles.summary: A building boom is under way in Medora.

articles.text: The cool mornings of the past week indicates for a certainty the near approach of grim winter. A few weeks more and our verdant hills and vales will be covered by a blanket of "pure and spotless"—snow. Let her come. We have plenty of coal and a boy to shove it into the silver-mounted heater that graces our sanctum.
articles.summary: Cool mornings signal approaching winter.

articles.text: The railroad company is making a crossing over the track, which is a much needed improvement, but it is located two blocks from the stage office and freight depot and entirely out of the business part of the town, on an alley leading to the rear of the lumber yard and the company's stable. If a crossing is to be made it should be near the warehouse.
articles.summary: The Northern Pacific is building a track crossing that the paper says is in the wrong spot.

articles.text: The editors of the Independent and Times at Glendive are complimenting one another by calling each other "liars," "thieves" and other choice names. It is rumored that the Times man carries a small arsenal in his hip pocket, and the residents of that enterprising city seem impressed with the belief that "bullud" will be shed.
articles.summary: Packard pokes fun at the feud between the Glendive Independent and Times editors.

articles.text: A. T. Packard, editor of the Cow Boy, and the rustling general manager of the new stage line from Medora to Deadwood, left Sunday morning for Pierre to attend the Republican territorial convention as a delegate. A. T. grows eloquent at times and will doubtless do some effective mouth-work while attempting to paralyze the political aspirations of ——— ———. Mr. Packard will return by way of Deadwood and will reach Medora about the 30 inst.
articles.summary: Editor A. T. Packard, general manager of the Medora–Deadwood stage line, left Sunday for Pierre as a delegate and will return by way of Deadwood about Sept. 30.

articles.text: The active and energetic managers of the Medora stage and forwarding company are indefatigable in their efforts to improve as far as possible the really natural road between this place and Deadwood, and in a short time freight will begin to roll steadily over the new route. Already trains are being loaded here with freight. The large and elegant coaches are models of beauty and and convey passengers to and fro with but little more discomfort than is encountered by the Pullman car tourist.
articles.summary: The Medora Stage and Forwarding Company is improving the Deadwood road; freight trains are already loading at Medora.

articles.headline: Notice of Dissolution.
articles.text:
Medora, September 13, 1884.
Notice is hereby given that the firm of Coleman & Brown is this day mutually dissolved, M. M. Coleman continuing the business. All claims due and against the late firm must be settled by the said M. M. Coleman, unless fraudulently contracted.
M. M. Coleman,
C. F. Brown.

Springfield Fire & Marine Ins. Co., Springfield, Mass. — A. T. Packard, Agent, Bad Lands Cow Boy office, Medora, Dak.

Brick!! made at the Medora Brick Kiln — "Only $8 Per Thousand!"; Peter J. Book, Medora, Dak.
Lots! Lots in Medora — table of lots and prices; for sale at the office of the Bad Lands Cow Boy, A. T. Packard, Medora, Dak.
Beef Cattle for sale — about 700 she cattle and 250 steers, plus 65 bulls and 55 she cattle, on Beaver creek, Dawson county, Montana, ten miles north of Keith; N. P. Ref. Car Co., Medora, Dak.

Wise & Goodkind, Bismarck, Dak. — wholesale wines, liquors, cigars

Brand: Clark & Plum, Spearfish, Dakota — E6 on left side; $100 reward for information on anyone killing or driving stock from the VVV or E6 ranges
Brand: H. R. Tarbell & Co., Medora — HT horse brand on left shoulder; range Davis creek and Little Missouri river
Brand: W. N. Thompson & Co., Wm. Dantz, Manager, P.O. Medora — TD on left hip
Brand: Lemoyne Cattle Co. (Limited), D. K. Wade, Manager, Medora — LC on left side; range Little Missouri, south of the R. R.; ranch Tepee bottom

articles.summary: Directory of display advertisers and cattle-brand ads on page 4.

events.date_basis: "last Monday" before Thu 18 Sep 1884
events.title: Fall round-up begins
events.summary: The fall round-up began on Monday.
events.excerpt: The fall round-up commenced last Monday.

events.date_basis: "Sunday" before Thu 18 Sep 1884
events.title: Packard leaves for the Pierre convention as a delegate
events.summary: A. T. Packard, editor and general manager of the new Medora–Deadwood stage line, left Sunday morning for Pierre to attend the Republican territorial convention as a delegate.
events.excerpt: left Sunday morning for Pierre to attend the Republican territorial convention as a delegate.

events.date_basis: "about the 30 inst." in the 18 Sep 1884 issue
events.title: Packard expected back in Medora by way of Deadwood
events.summary: Packard was to return from Pierre by way of Deadwood, reaching Medora about Sept. 30.
events.excerpt: Mr. Packard will return by way of Deadwood and will reach Medora about the 30 inst.

events.date_basis: "met yesterday" before Thu 18 Sep 1884
events.title: Republican territorial convention opens at Pierre
events.summary: The Republican territorial convention met at Pierre to nominate a delegate to congress. A fight was expected against incumbent John B. Raymond, with Samuel McMaster of Deadwood favored by the paper; 52 North Dakota delegates, Billings county's two among them, were reported refusing to join the Raymond caucus.
events.excerpt: The Republican territorial convention met yesterday at Pierre to nominate a delegate to congress.

events.date_basis: "Monday evening, September 22" stated in notice
events.title: Republican county convention called at Medora
events.summary: J. C. Fisher, county central committee chairman, called a Republican convention at Roberts' hall, Medora, for 7 p.m. Sept. 22 to elect two Billings county delegates to the legislative convention at Bismarck on Oct. 15.
events.excerpt: a Republican convention will be held at Medora, Dak., Monday evening, September 22, at 7 o'clock, in Roberts' hall

events.date_basis: certificate "Dated, Medora, D. T., Sept. 8, 1884"
events.title: Packard and Deffebach form the Medora Stage and Forwarding Company
events.summary: A certificate of copartnership recorded that Arthur T. Packard and Erasmus Deffebach had formed the Medora Stage and Forwarding Company, with its place of business at Medora. Notary Frank B. Allen witnessed it.
events.excerpt: we have this day entered into copartnership under the name of the "Medora Stage and Forwarding Company,"

events.date_basis: "this morning" in the Thu 18 Sep 1884 issue
events.title: Supt. Deffebach brings stage horses from Helena
events.summary: Supt. Deffebach of the Medora Stage and Forwarding Company returned from Helena with eleven head of horses for the stage line.
events.excerpt: returned from Helena this morning with eleven head of horses for the stage line.

events.date_basis: no date given; week before Thu 18 Sep 1884
events.title: Stage company manager J. C. Fisher gets an office
events.summary: J. C. Fisher, local manager of the stage company, moved into an office partitioned off from the large warehouse.
events.excerpt: is nicely ensconced in a cozy office which has been partitioned off from the large warehouse.

events.date_basis: "yesterday" before Thu 18 Sep 1884
events.title: Jorgens and Vic Smith inspect the stage route; shorter road found
events.summary: H. M. Jorgens and Vic Smith returned from inspecting the stage route. The week before, Smith had found a route from the Davis creek station to the Rocky Ridge station along a divide with a natural gravel road-bed. Lumber for two more stations was being sent out.
events.excerpt: Vic is the pathfinder, and last week discovored a route from the first station on Davis creek to the second on Rocky Ridge

events.date_basis: no date given; week before Thu 18 Sep 1884
events.title: Stage company improving the Medora–Deadwood road
events.summary: The paper said the stage company's managers were improving the road to Deadwood, freight trains were already loading at Medora, and steady freight traffic would start soon.
events.excerpt: Already trains are being loaded here with freight.

events.date_basis: no date given; week before Thu 18 Sep 1884
events.title: Stage horses shod and sent along the line
events.summary: Stage horses were being shod and distributed along the stage line.
events.excerpt: The stage horses are being shod as rapidly as possible and distributed along the line.

events.date_basis: "this week" in the 18 Sep 1884 issue
events.title: Gill Kennedy paints the stage coaches
events.summary: Gill Kennedy was painting the stage coaches.
events.excerpt: Gill Kennedy is decorating the stage coaches with a coat of paint

events.date_basis: "this week" in the Thu 18 Sep 1884 issue
events.title: Stage driver Bill Luse arrives from Montana
events.summary: Bill Luse, an experienced Montana stage driver, arrived in town to drive for the stage company.
events.excerpt: Bill Luse, an experienced stage driver of Montana, arrived in town this week.

events.date_basis: "in a few days" from 18 Sep 1884
events.title: Baron and Baroness von Hoffman expected back
events.summary: The Baron and Baroness von Hoffman were expected to return from their western trip within a few days.
events.excerpt: are expected to return from their western trip in a few days.

events.date_basis: no date given; correction of the previous issue
events.title: Baroness von Hoffmann's brick cottage is a gift to Mr. Grymes
events.summary: Correcting the last issue, the paper said the new brick cottage the Baroness von Hoffmann is building is a present for Mr. Grymes.
events.excerpt: Mr. Grymes is the happy recipient of the Baroness' valuable present.

events.date_basis: no date given; correction of the previous issue
events.title: New church to be built by the Marchioness de Morès
events.summary: Correcting the last issue, the paper said the new church will be built by the Marchioness, not the Marquis.
events.excerpt: The new church is to be built by the Marchioness instead of the Marquis, as stated in last week's paper.

events.date_basis: ready-print "Dakota News Notes" item in the 18 Sep 1884 issue; no date given
events.title: Territorial notes credit the Marquis de Morès with the Medora–Deadwood stage line
events.summary: A syndicated Dakota news item said the Marquis de Morès had organized a stage line from Medora, on the Northern Pacific, to Deadwood.
events.excerpt: A stage line has been organized by Marquis de Mores to run from Medora, on the Northern Pacific railroad, to Deadwood.

events.date_basis: "this week" in the Thu 18 Sep 1884 issue
events.title: J. L. Crooks drives in 126 horses for H. R. Tarbell & Co.
events.summary: J. L. Crooks of Spearfish drove 126 head of horses in for H. R. Tarbell & Co.
events.excerpt: drove in this week 126 head of horses for H. R. Tarbell & Co.

events.date_basis: "this week" in the Thu 18 Sep 1884 issue
events.title: E. W. Crane of Emigrant Gulch visits
events.summary: E. W. Crane of Emigrant Gulch, Mont., was in town.
events.excerpt: E. W. Crane, of Emigrant Gulch, Mont., was in town this week.

events.date_basis: "yesterday" before Thu 18 Sep 1884
events.title: Government surveyor Duryea in town
events.summary: Mr. Duryea of the government surveying party was in town.
events.excerpt: Mr. Duryea, of the government surveying party, was in town yesterday.

events.date_basis: "last week" before Thu 18 Sep 1884
events.title: C. D. Edick of Bismarck visits
events.summary: Bismarck cigar manufacturer C. D. Edick was in town.
events.excerpt: C. D. Edick, cigar manufacturer of Bismarck, was in town last week.

events.date_basis: "this week" in the Thu 18 Sep 1884 issue
events.title: T. M. Wright, formerly of the Bismarck Tribune, visits
events.summary: T. M. Wright, formerly of the Bismarck Tribune, spent a few days in town.
events.excerpt: was in town a few days this week.

events.date_basis: "last evening's" train, before Thu 18 Sep 1884
events.title: Supt. Green of the Missouri division passes through
events.summary: Supt. Green of the Northern Pacific's Missouri division passed through on the westbound passenger train.
events.excerpt: passed through on last evening's west bound passenger.

events.date_basis: no date given; week before Thu 18 Sep 1884
events.title: J. A. Ferris adds groceries to his store
events.summary: Merchant J. A. Ferris added a complete stock of groceries to his general store.
events.excerpt: has added a complete stock of groceries to his general store.

events.date_basis: notice dated "Medora, September 13, 1884"
events.title: Coleman & Brown dissolve partnership in the Medora hotel
events.summary: Coleman & Brown, proprietors of the Medora hotel, dissolved their partnership, and M. M. Coleman continues the business.
events.excerpt: have dissolved partnership, M. M. Coleman continuing the business.

events.date_basis: "Sunday" before Thu 18 Sep 1884
events.title: Railroad carpenter robbed at Dickinson
events.summary: One of the railroad carpenters went to Dickinson and, while drunk, was robbed of his watch and pocketbook.
events.excerpt: while under the influence of tanglefoot was rolled for his watch and pocket-book.

events.date_basis: no date given; week before Thu 18 Sep 1884
events.title: Dr. H. M. Jorgens awaits his drug stock
events.summary: Dr. H. M. Jorgens was expecting his drug stock; the building he will use for now was moved next to the company's store.
events.excerpt: The building which he is to occupy temporarily has been moved next to the company's store.

events.date_basis: no date given; week before Thu 18 Sep 1884
events.title: Frank Turner overhauls the abattoir machinery
events.summary: Frank Turner was overhauling the abattoir machinery between killings.
events.excerpt: Frank Turner is overhauling the machinery in the abattoir

events.date_basis: "Tuesday evening" before Thu 18 Sep 1884
events.title: John Norton returns from St. Paul after a dressed-beef shipment
events.summary: John Norton returned from St. Paul, where he had taken several carloads of the company's dressed beef, and said they arrived in excellent condition.
events.excerpt: whither he had gone with several carloads of the company's dressed beef.

events.date_basis: no date given; week before Thu 18 Sep 1884
events.title: Experimental refrigerator car "Antartic" shipped with beef
events.summary: The company loaded a new refrigerator car, the "Antartic," with beef as an experiment and shipped it in care of the builder. If it works, more cars will be built.
events.excerpt: A new refrigerator car, the "Antartic," was loaded with beef by the company, as an experiment

events.date_basis: "last Monday" before Thu 18 Sep 1884
events.title: Pat O'Hara's coal mine running again
events.summary: Pat O'Hara came in from the stage route; his coal mine was running in full blast again, and orders could be left at the Cow Boy office.
events.excerpt: He has the coal mine running in full blast again

events.date_basis: no date given; week before Thu 18 Sep 1884
events.title: Building boom in Medora
events.summary: The paper reported new and attractive buildings going up in every part of town and expected the boom to continue for two or three months.
events.excerpt: New and attractive buildings are going up in every part of town

events.date_basis: "the past week" before Thu 18 Sep 1884
events.title: Cool mornings signal approaching winter
events.summary: The paper noted cool mornings over the past week as a sign that winter was near.
events.excerpt: The cool mornings of the past week indicates for a certainty the near approach of grim winter.

events.date_basis: no date given; week before Thu 18 Sep 1884
events.title: Railroad builds a track crossing at Medora
events.summary: The railroad company was building a crossing over the track two blocks from the stage office and freight depot. The paper argued it belonged near the warehouse.
events.excerpt: The railroad company is making a crossing over the track, which is a much needed improvement

events.date_basis: no date given; week before Thu 18 Sep 1884
events.title: Glendive newspaper editors feud
events.summary: The paper reported that the editors of the Glendive Independent and Times were calling each other liars and thieves.
events.excerpt: are complimenting one another by calling each other "liars," "thieves" and other choice names.

events.date_basis: no date given; week before Thu 18 Sep 1884
events.title: Ranchers offer $250 reward against grass-fire setters
events.summary: Western Dakota cattle outfits, including the N. P. Ref. Car Co., Continental Cattle Co., Dorr Clark and E. G. Paddock, offered $250 for information leading to the arrest of anyone setting the range grass on fire.
events.excerpt: information leading to the arrest of any person or persons setting fire to the grass in the cattle sections of Western Dakota.

events.date_basis: no date given; week before Thu 18 Sep 1884
events.title: Gregor Lang offers reward for strayed horses
events.summary: Gregor Lang of Medora offered $50 for the return of three young mares branded P and a sorrel pony branded NC and JP.
events.excerpt: One bay mare, one brown mare and one roan mare, all young and branded double or reverse P on left shoulder

events.date_basis: "Sept. 20" stated (clipped from Glendive Times)
events.title: Standard Cattle Company orders cars at Mingusville
events.summary: The Glendive Times reported that the Standard Cattle Company of Wyoming had ordered fifty cars at Mingusville for Sept. 20 to ship its herd, and Harris & Clevinger wanted twenty cars there on the 25th.
events.excerpt: have ordered fifty cars at Mingusville, Sept. 20, to accommodate their herd now on the drive for shipment.

events.date_basis: clipping from Black Hills Pioneer, no date resolvable
events.title: Dorr Clark reports sick cattle in through herds
events.summary: In a Black Hills Pioneer item, Dorr Clark said many sick cattle were in late through herds, but cattlemen's quarantine was keeping the disease from the range cattle.
events.excerpt: there are many sick cattle among some of the late through herds, but they are so effectually quarantined by the cattle men
